newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly up.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on stable market sentiment, and investors liquidated large positions in the March contract ahead of the delivery date, traders said.
The key September 1997 contract ended at 3,332 yuan ($401) per tonne, rising five yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,320 yuan and hit a high of 3,334 yuan per tonne.
March fell 43 to 3,137, May and July did not trade, November rose 10 to 3,342 and January 1998 was up eight to 3,348.
Combined volume rose to 47,900 tonnes from 25,000.
Most soybean contracts opened lower but rebounded steadily for most of the session because few investors were willing to sell at current low prices with fundamentals improving, traders said.
"Market sentiment was stable after corrections over the past few days, helping the day's gains," one trader said.
"Investors offset most positions in the March contract with no intention of taking delivery," he added.
The March 1997 contract will expire next Tuesday.
